Instrument: Sheikh JI & Yesavage JA (1986) Clin Gerontol 5:165-173; Dutch translation Bleeker, Frohn de Winter & Cornelissen (1985).
note: CODE DERIVATION: data/depue_2023_covid_older_adults.py melts the deposit columns GDS1..GDS15 (T1) and M2_GDSk/M3_GDSk (T2/T3, prefix stripped) BY NAME -- the IRW code IS the source column name, no positional step. NO LABELS: both deposits are plain ';'-delimited CSVs with bare headers (no variable or value labels); both ReadThisFirst.txt files say only 'Column 57 to 71 (GDS1 to GDS15): 15 recoded (based on the GDS-15 recoding scheme) items of the Geriatric Depression Scale-15 (GDS-15; Sheikh & Yesavage, 1986; Bleeker, Frohn de Winter, & Cornelissen, 1985)'; neither paper nor either supplementary .docx reproduces any GDS item. So GDSk -> canonical GDS-15 item k is RECONSTRUCTED from the instrument numbering and then checked against the data (verify_depue_2023_gds15.R, PARTIAL). LANGUAGE: 'The language of the survey was Dutch' (2021 paper, Methods). No Dutch GDS wording is in either OSF deposit, either supplement or either paper (checked all six files + both PMC full texts), so this is the translated_substitute fallback: Yesavage's English short form ships in the base fields with language=Dutch and no _translated columns. The Dutch items are Bleeker et al.'s translation of the same 15 numbered items; not compared word-for-word. TEXT: stems and instructions ('Choose the best answer for how you have felt over the past week:') transcribed verbatim from the Stanford page (the instrument's own framing, not the study's, which did not publish its instructions); 'YES'/'NO' in the source's capitals. RESP: stored key-scored, 1 = the depressive answer (Stanford page bold: NO for items 1,5,7,11,13, YES for the rest), so option_text maps resp 1 -> NO for those five items and resp 1 -> YES for the other ten. Evidence: ReadThisFirst 'recoded (based on the GDS-15 recoding scheme)'; the paper's 'Using a score key, each item receives a score of 0 or 1'; all 15 T1 item-rest r positive (+0.16..+0.69), which raw YES=1 storage would violate for the five positive items; every published total reproduced exactly (2021 N=640 3.00 (3.01); 2023 n=371 T1 2.60 (2.66), T2 2.59 (2.80), T3 2.77 (2.80); T1 drop-outs 3.56 (3.37); alphas .81/.78/.80/.80). RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv GDS row verdict 'ship' (Ben 2026-09-23) applied: 'The original scale is in the public domain due to it being partly the result of Federal support.' -- page re-fetched today, sha256 unchanged. Register verdict not re-derived. COUNTS: 15 items x 2 = 30 rows; live 20,729 rows, 1,382 per item except GDS11 1,381 (one T1 respondent skipped it; not a defect).
public_note: Respondents answered the Dutch translation of the GDS-15 but the item text shown is Yesavage's original English, and responses are stored key-scored (1 = the depressive answer), so for items GDS1, GDS5, GDS7, GDS11 and GDS13 a 1 means the respondent answered NO
